settings.body:
Use Wedding Photo for save-the-date concepts, ceremony moodboards, invitation-friendly portraits, wedding website visuals, or private keepsakes. Prepare approved photos of both people, choose one ceremony direction, and treat every result as wedding-inspired creative imagery rather than proof of a real event.

Choose the wedding use before the visual style

A save-the-date needs text-safe composition. A ceremony moodboard can explore atmosphere, clothing, floral direction, and light. An invitation portrait should leave room for verified copy. A website header needs a wide crop that survives navigation overlays. A private keepsake can favor emotion and close detail.

Choose Wedding Photo when formal couple styling, ceremony atmosphere, floral details, or card-ready framing is central. Choose Engagement for a proposal or ring-led announcement. Choose Valentine's Day for a seasonal romantic card that does not make a ceremony claim.

Prepare both people and one ceremony direction

Use recent, clear portraits of both people with similar lighting and useful face angles. Confirm that each person approves the source images, generated pairing, intended audience, and final use. Then choose one direction: ceremony, formal studio, outdoor romance, or card-ready portrait.

Include only cultural, floral, wardrobe, jewelry, and ceremonial details that knowledgeable participants can review accurately. Do not invent family traditions, religious meaning, or event facts that were not supplied.

Match the theme to the relationship claim

ThemePrimary formatBoundary
Wedding PhotoCeremony-led concepts, formal portraits, save-the-dates, and keepsakesDo not present generated imagery as event documentation.
Engagement PhotoProposal, ring, and announcement-led imageryThe announcement and relationship claim must be real and approved.
Valentine's DaySeasonal romantic cards, date-night portraits, and giftsUse seasonal language without implying a ceremony.

Review the live Wedding Photo package card for current outputs and credit cost.

Add names, dates, and venue copy later

Leave names, dates, venue details, invitation copy, and schedules out of the generated scene. Add verified text later in a design tool where spelling, hierarchy, and date accuracy can be controlled. A clean text-safe crop is more reliable than generated lettering that appears correct at first glance.

Review consent, ceremony details, and pair anatomy

Use generated wedding images as concepts or keepsakes, not as proof that a ceremony, venue booking, marriage, or cultural rite occurred. Share couple images only with both people's approval.

  • Check both faces, eye direction, expression, and relative scale.
  • Inspect overlapping hands and arms, rings, jewelry, and bouquet stems.
  • Review veil and hair edges, suit and dress fabric, and floral repetition.
  • Check ceremonial objects, cultural details, background guests, and venue cues.
  • Confirm the final card or website crop preserves text-safe spacing.
  • Have knowledgeable participants review meaningful attire, symbols, and rituals.

AI wedding portrait FAQ

Can a generated wedding portrait document a real ceremony?

No. Use it as a concept, moodboard, invitation-friendly visual, or keepsake. Real event claims require real documentation.

Who should approve a couple image?

Both people should approve the source photos, generated pairing, relationship claim, intended audience, and final use.

Where should names and dates be added?

Add verified copy after generation in a design tool so spelling, dates, hierarchy, and placement can be controlled.

How should cultural details be reviewed?

Include only details supplied by the participants and ask knowledgeable people to review attire, symbols, rituals, and ceremonial objects before publication.

settings.title: How credits work

settings.body:
1. Agreement to these terms

These Terms of Service apply when you visit www.mydreamshoots.com, create a myDreamshoots account, upload photos, buy credits or subscriptions, use AI photo tools, start generation jobs, download outputs, or access private albums.

2. Accounts, credits, and checkout

You are responsible for accurate account information and secure sign-in. Credits are added after payment confirmation, displayed before generation, reserved when a request begins, used after successful delivery, and released or reviewed when a request fails.

3. Upload rights and consent

You may upload only photos, reference images, prompts, or other materials that you own or have permission to use. Do not upload minors, non-consenting people, public figures, protected marks, stolen images, or materials that violate law, platform rules, or third-party rights.

4. Photo-use terms

The current policy describes how inputs are handled for service delivery; confirm the live Privacy Policy and provider terms before relying on a retention or training assumption. Input-photo retention applies to input photos after generation. Private uploads and account records are protected by secure account, storage, and access workflows. Some billing, security, tax, dispute, refund, and account-integrity records may be retained where required or reasonably necessary.

5. AI output variability

AI photo results can vary based on source photo quality, pose, lighting, package settings, moderation review, provider availability, and model behavior. myDreamshoots may reject, rerun, delay, moderate, or remove jobs that violate rules or cannot be completed reliably.

6. Private albums and use of outputs

Generated images and albums are designed for private customer access unless you choose to share, publish, or download them. You are responsible for reviewing outputs before using them in advertising, profiles, documents, merchandise, social media, or other public settings.

7. Refunds and guarantee review

Refunds and credit adjustments follow the Refund Policy, including refund review when the shoot does not look like you, subject to support review, account history, and the details of the affected request.

8. Contact

Email support@mydreamshoots.com for account, billing, refund, policy, or legal questions.

settings.title: How cookies support sign-in, checkout, and private albums.

settings.body:
1. What cookies are

Cookies are small files stored by your browser. myDreamshoots also uses similar browser storage, such as local storage, to keep the AI photo service secure, usable, and consistent while you move between packages, checkout, your account, and private albums.

2. Essential cookies

Essential cookies support customer sign-in, scoped sessions, CSRF protection, checkout continuity, credit reservation flows, private album access, rate limiting, fraud prevention, and secure admin or customer authentication. These cookies are required for the core service and cannot be switched off inside the site without breaking key features.

3. Preference storage

We may remember practical preferences such as menu state, recently opened workspace views, selected package context, language or display choices if available, and browser-side UI settings. This helps myDreamshoots open the right customer workspace more quickly.

4. Performance and diagnostics

We may collect limited technical signals to understand slow pages, failed requests, broken checkout steps, job submission errors, and account access issues. These signals help us improve route speed, generation reliability, and customer support.

5. Analytics and measurement

If analytics tools are enabled, they may help us understand aggregated usage such as popular package categories, tool discovery, pricing page visits, and conversion paths. Analytics should not be used to sell your uploaded photos or generated images.

6. Payment, email, hosting, and AI providers

Connected providers may set or read cookies or similar identifiers when needed for checkout, anti-fraud checks, email delivery, hosting security, media storage, or AI generation. Their use is limited to providing and protecting the requested service.

7. Your browser controls

You can block, delete, or limit cookies in your browser settings. If you block essential cookies, myDreamshoots may not be able to keep you signed in, complete checkout, reserve credits, start generation jobs, or open private albums.

8. Relationship to privacy policy

Cookie data is handled together with the privacy practices described in our Privacy Policy. The Terms of Service explain customer responsibilities when using accounts, credits, uploads, and generated outputs.

9. Updates and contact

We may update this Cookie Policy as we add or remove providers, analytics, checkout methods, or security features. Email support@mydreamshoots.com with cookie or tracking questions.

The Soccer package category helps myDreamshoots customers choose a clear package direction before they spend credits.

When Soccer is the right fit

Use Soccer when Soccer and Sports are the nearest match for the next photo set. If the goal is still vague, start by naming the final use: profile update, creator album, keepsake, announcement, social draft, or a short motion test.

The strongest soccer requests keep the brief and the result aligned. A customer who needs a calm work portrait should not judge the same set by the standards of a dramatic scene package.

What to prepare before choosing it

Prepare clear approved source portraits, then add one cue that belongs to Soccer: light, scene texture, outfit tone, occasion, group size, or card-ready crop. Start with sharp source photos and one style cue that matters most to the package. Treat the source photos as identity evidence first. Style references, outfit notes, fan details, holiday cues, or movement ideas should support the request after the person is already clear.

For a first pass, keep the input set smaller and cleaner than a social camera roll. Use current images, avoid heavy filters, and separate unrelated goals into different private jobs. myDreamshoots can follow a focused brief more reliably than a folder that asks for several looks at once.

How to compare Soccer with nearby choices

Compare soccer against neighboring packages by the job it solves, not by which cover image looks strongest. The table below turns the category into a practical choice before credit cost is confirmed.

Decision pointUse Soccer whenReview after generation
Final useUse Soccer when Sports is the right broad direction and the private album needs the specific look, scene, or keepsake format described by Soccer.Review whether the finished images look like Soccer instead of drifting into a generic Sports album.
source photosPrepare clear approved source portraits, then add one cue that belongs to Soccer: light, scene texture, outfit tone, occasion, group size, or card-ready crop.Check whether the clearest input details carried through the best images.
Category examplesSoccer and SportsKeep the outputs that match the chosen example instead of mixing several directions.
Credit planUse a focused first pass when the style is new.Decide whether the next request should repeat, expand, or change direction.

Credit and private gallery planning

Before the job starts, review the visible credit cost and ask whether the category is carrying the right amount of work. If you only need to test soccer, a smaller request can teach you what works. If the final use is already clear, a broader gallery may be easier to judge because it gives more crops and expressions to compare.

Finished outputs belong in the signed-in private gallery first. Use that space to compare identity, crop, expression, background detail, and whether the package category actually delivered the mood you selected. Download favorites only after separating public-use images from experiments.

Details to review before download

Review whether the finished images look like Soccer instead of drifting into a generic Sports album. Also check small visual details that often decide whether a result is ready for a profile, card, post, or archive: face consistency, hand and hair edges, clothing lines, background distractions, and whether the image still reads well at the crop size where you will use it.

Soccer should be recognizable through visible details such as color, posture, card framing, scene texture, seasonal cues, supporter energy, or private keepsake mood. This is where Soccer becomes more than a menu label. The visible mood should explain why the category was chosen, while the private gallery keeps the customer in control of what stays personal and what becomes a downloaded favorite.

Mistakes to avoid

Avoid asking Soccer to cover several unrelated fan, game-day, premiere, or holiday scenes at once; the narrower theme should make review easier. The fastest way to weaken soccer results is to overload the request with unrelated goals. Do not ask one job to be a professional portrait, a themed album, a restoration pass, and a motion concept at the same time. Keep the category honest, then run a second request when the next direction is different enough to need its own review.

A planning pass before you spend credits

  • Name the exact use for the finished images.
  • Choose the clearest source photos before adding style references.
  • Match the request to Soccer and Sports, not every nearby category.
  • Review credit cost before generation starts.
  • Use the private gallery to compare results before downloading favorites.

Start with Headshot Photo Package, then compare Soccer with nearby categories before generating. The best choice is the one that makes the review criteria obvious before the first image is generated.

Soccer FAQ

Soccer questions usually come down to source quality, scope, credit planning, and whether the finished images match the intended use.

Is Soccer good for a first request?

Yes, if the intended use is clear and the source photos are current, sharp, and permission-safe. If you are testing a dramatic change, start narrower so the first private gallery can show whether the direction deserves a larger credit spend.

How many source photos should I prepare?

Use enough images to show identity, angle, and expression without adding confusion. A small set of clear portraits usually beats a large group of old, filtered, or mixed-purpose images.

When should I choose another category instead?

Choose another category when the review criteria change. If Soccer is being judged by a different use case, style world, or motion need, split the work into a separate private job so credits support a clearer outcome.

Soccer works best when it is treated as a focused planning choice. Prepare the right inputs, review the cost, and let the private gallery show what should happen next.

1. Service audience

myDreamshoots is not directed to children under 13 and is not designed for child account creation. Customers should use the service only if they can lawfully manage an account or have permission from a parent or legal guardian.

2. COPPA-aware handling

The Children's Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA) applies to certain online services directed to children under 13 or knowingly collecting personal information from children under 13. myDreamshoots does not knowingly collect account information directly from children under 13. If we learn that child personal information was provided without required consent, we will review and delete or restrict it as appropriate.

3. Photos of minors

Customers must not upload photos of minors unless they are the parent, legal guardian, or otherwise have the legal right and consent to use those images for the requested AI workflow. Minor images should never be used for deceptive, exploitative, unlawful, or unsafe purposes.

4. Parent or guardian requests

A parent or legal guardian may contact us to ask about access, deletion, or restriction of child-related information. We may request verification before acting on a sensitive privacy request.

5. DPDPA requests

California and other U.S. state privacy requests are handled in our DPDPA notice, including access, deletion, correction, opt-out, and appeal requests where applicable.

2. COPPA-aware handling

The Children's Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA) applies to certain online services directed to children under 13 or knowingly collecting personal information from children under 13. myDreamshoots does not knowingly collect account information directly from children under 13. If we learn that child personal information was provided without required consent, we will review and delete or restrict it as appropriate.

3. Photos of minors

Customers must not upload photos of minors unless they are the parent, legal guardian, or otherwise have the legal right and consent to use those images for the requested AI workflow. Minor images should never be used for deceptive, exploitative, unlawful, or unsafe purposes.

4. Parent or guardian requests

A parent or legal guardian may contact us to ask about access, deletion, or restriction of child-related information. We may request verification before acting on a sensitive privacy request.

5. DPDPA requests

California and other U.S. state privacy requests are handled in our DPDPA notice, including access, deletion, correction, opt-out, and appeal requests where applicable.

6. Contact

Email support@mydreamshoots.com for children's privacy or COPPA-related questions.
